subject: Pricing slate: threshold buffer & packaging alignment (redlines)
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@nebulahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: NH redlines - pricing schedule + packaging table

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached is Nebula Health's consolidated redline to the order form pricing schedule and packaging table (NH_pricing_redlines_v2.docx). The key asks we flagged are:

- A clarified "threshold buffer" that protects Nebula from an immediate step-up if usage spikes in the first billing quarter.
- A request to replace the proposed "annual true-up" floor with a quarterly reconciliation window for the first 12 months.
- Packaging alignment: we want one SKU for "clinical batch embedding" across regions instead of separate EU/US SKUs to simplify billing.

We've annotated the redline with rationale in comments. We understand Redwood's desire for predictability; these tweaks are our risk-mitigation asks while we accelerate initial usage.

Attached: NH_pricing_redlines_v2.docx (redline), sample invoice illustrative table.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the threshold-floor language discussion?

Thanks,
Anika Shah
Head of Procurement, Nebula Health
Anika.Shah@nebulahealth.com

---
Attachment: NH_pricing_redlines_v2.docx (Microsoft Word redline, 183KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NH redlines - pricing schedule + packaging table

Anika —

Appreciate the clear redline and the notes. I'll own the commercial side and loop Legal as needed. Quick read-through notes up front:

- Threshold buffer: we can propose a 15% smoothing buffer for the first 90 days rather than a straight floor; that preserves throughput guarantees but avoids an immediate billing cliff.
- Quarterly reconciliation for the first year is reasonable, but we need to confirm cashflow/commit implications with Finance.
- Single SKU packaging across regions may be OK if we add a clause for regionally-applied tax and regulatory surcharges.

I've attached initial counter-notes (Karthik_countertrack_notes.txt) with line references. Marcus — can you take point on the packaging SKU language and propose precise phrasing we can share back? Lauren — I'll expect a quick pricing impact estimate when you have 24h.

I'll send a tracked-change version of the order form once we consolidate.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Karthik_countertrack_notes.txt (plain text, 5KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NH redlines - pricing schedule + packaging table

Karthik / Lauren —

Looping in suggested language below (pulled into this thread to keep a single source of truth). Happy to iterate.

Quoted: 
> "Packaging alignment: we want one SKU for 'clinical batch embedding' across regions instead of separate EU/US SKUs to simplify billing."

Proposed phrasing for order form: 
"Clinical Batch Embedding SKU: The Parties agree to a single product SKU for 'Clinical Batch Embedding' (the 'Consolidated SKU') for the Term. Billing will use the Consolidated SKU; regionally applicable taxes, regulatory surcharges, and usage-based network fees shall be listed as separate line items and shall not change the unit price of the Consolidated SKU. Redwood reserves the right to apply region-specific regulatory pass-throughs with 30 days' prior notice to Customer."

On the threshold buffer: suggest replacing '15% smoothing buffer' with an explicit matrix in Exhibit B that defines: 0-90 days => 15% buffer, 91-365 days => 10% buffer, after 365 days => standard thresholds. That makes escalation deterministic.

I'll draft tracked changes and attach.

Marcus
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Marcus_packaging_track.docx (proposed tracked changes, 12KB)

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@nebulahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika.shah@nebulahealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Dec 2026 14:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NH redlines - pricing schedule + packaging table

Karthik / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and proposed language. A couple of counterpoints from our finance team:

1) The matrix is helpful, but we'd prefer the 15% buffer apply to the first full invoice period (first 30 days) rather than 90 days — our usage tends to spike on initial onboarding weeks. Could we change the matrix to 30/120/365 windows (15%/12%/8%)?

2) On the Consolidated SKU: agreeable in principle, but Nebula requests a 6-month review clause to adjust unit pricing if there's a material (>25%) change in aggregate cross-region usage patterns. The intent is to avoid being locked into an inappropriate unit price if workloads shift dramatically.

I've attached a lightly edited order form with the requested changes (Nebula_NH-OrderForm_v3.pdf) and included an excerpt that shows where we'd add the 6-month review.

Can Redwood confirm whether the 6-month review would require mutual written agreement to change pricing (vs unilateral adjustment)? That distinction is important for our CFO.

Best,
Tom Reed
VP, Cloud Procurement, Nebula Health

---
Attachment: Nebula_NH-OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF with inline annotations, 114KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@nebulahealth.com>, Anika Shah <anika.shah@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NH redlines - pricing schedule + packaging table

Tom / Anika —

Thanks — this is constructive. Quick confirmations and next steps so we can close the order form: 

- Buffer windows: Redwood can accept the 30/120/365 window but requests the percentages you proposed be the starting point and that we include the matrix in Exhibit B with explicit triggers. We'll add language that any changes to the matrix require mutual written agreement.

- 6-month review: Redwood is fine with a 6-month commercial review clause on the Consolidated SKU; any pricing changes resulting from that review will require mutual written agreement and 30 days' lead time before taking effect. We'll add a safe harbor that prevents retroactive repricing for charges already invoiced.

- Consolidated SKU: Marcus's suggested pass-through language stands; we'll add an explicit line-item for regional surcharges.

Attached I am sending a consolidated tracked version (final draft) with all agreed items (redwood_NH_orderform_consolidated_v1.docx). Once legal confirms the language, I'll route this to your procurement team for signature; Anika, if DocuSign is fine I can send the envelope via the link below.

DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/nebula/ENVELOPE-123456789

Marcus / Lauren / Legal: please confirm the attached text is final by end-of-day Wednesday so we can hit the client's target.

Thanks and happy holidays,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
